notes.cutoff: Data cut-off: this edition covers Thursday evening to Sunday morning, before the EGX opens at 10:00. The latest EGX close is Thursday 19 November (EGX30 51,458.04). Wall Street, gold and oil are Friday 20 November closes. Gold prices in EGP are Banky's Sunday prices. Bullish and bearish tags are directional reads of the news, not trade recommendations.
notes.unverified: Not verified and therefore left out: Brent's exact Friday settlement ($92.57 from Reuters, $92.49 from Investing.com; the brief shows about $92.5 and flags the chart); Brent's weekly fall (3.5% or near 4%); Thursday's net flows by nationality, because Amwal Al Ghad reports non-Arab foreigners as net buyers of EGP 1.97 bn while EnterpriseAM reports international investors as the only net sellers; Thursday's breadth; the CBE's overnight lending rate, not stated on any page opened today; a CBE dollar rate newer than 18 November; the IRGC's claim to have destroyed two US Patriot radars; the date Orascom broke ground in Jordan. Egypt Aluminum's 17 November row on StockAnalysis remains inconsistent (a -0.30% change against a 5.2% fall in the closes).
notes.sourcesFoot: All 21 StockAnalysis pages opened on Sunday morning and show Thursday 19 November as the latest session.

items: Wall Street enters a correction: the Nasdaq falls 5.3% and the S&P 500 3.5% on Friday as the AI sell-off deepens → a global risk-off mood can weigh on emerging markets, including the EGX on Sunday.
Gold posts its worst week in eight months, down 8.9%, and 21K gold in Egypt drops 3.04% to EGP 5,575 → markets bet on a December Fed hike, and margin calls force sales.

Saudi-led coalition intercepts three Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh as Gulf war-risk costs climb → tanker insurance from the Middle East to Asia reaches $12.29 a barrel, keeping Red Sea and Suez risk high.
Arab Energy Fund launches a $70 mn tender offer for 21.3% of Maridive at $0.70 a share → a Gulf-backed buyer puts a price on an EGX-listed oil services firm.
An AI-led sell-off hits markets: the Nasdaq falls 2.3% on Thursday and Asian indices drop up to 6.8% on Friday → Anthropic's record IPO does not calm AI-bubble fears.
Egypt raises the private-sector minimum wage 21% to EGP 8,500 a month from 1 January 2027 → higher pay supports spending but raises costs for labour-heavy firms.
The EGX30 slips 0.17% to 51,458.04 as Telecom Egypt falls 3.47% → turnover is 43.9% below the 90-day average.
Gold drops to a 14-month low of $3,554 and heads for a 9% weekly loss → markets price a 97.3% chance of a Fed hike in December.

The IMF reaches a staff-level agreement on Egypt's final EFF review and third RSF review, worth about $2.3 bn → board approval before 15 December would close the programme and support the pound and Egypt's credit standing.
Egypt's economy grows 4.9% in July to September, up from 4.7%, while unemployment rises to 6.0% → growth holds up despite the war, rate hike and gas cuts.
Orascom Construction's nine-month profit nearly doubles to $218 mn as its backlog reaches $11.6 bn → strong awards support the stock ahead of the OCI merger listing on 24 November.
Gold falls 3.2% on Wednesday to its lowest close since September 2025; 21K in Egypt drops to EGP 5,750 → Fed minutes show almost all officials see more hikes ahead.

Misr Insurance Holding will sell 15% of Misr Life Insurance on the EGX in December, with EFG Hermes as sole bookrunner → the IMF wants about $1.5 bn of asset sales before the programme ends; Banque du Caire has delivered $658 mn so far.
EGX30 falls 0.99% to 51,682 on Tuesday and the EGX70 drops another 2.42% → local investors are the sole net sellers as small caps extend their slide.
Gold drops below $3,800 as Fed officials signal more rate hikes; 21K gold in Egypt slips to EGP 5,900 → higher US yields and a firm dollar weigh on bullion and on emerging-market carry.
The Arab Energy Fund files a $70 mn tender offer for 21.3% of Maridive at $0.70 a share → Gulf money keeps buying into EGX-listed energy services.

Seven fertiliser makers agree to pay 50% more for gas, $12.75 per mmBtu and $175 mn upfront, in return for exporting their full output until early January → the state recovers some LNG costs while producers keep selling urea at about $535 a tonne; gas cuts of 20-40% stay.
EGX30 ends flat at 52,200 on Monday but the EGX70 drops 3.76% and the EGX100 2.88% → small caps sell off while Edita (+7.4%) and Telecom Egypt (+5.2%) hold up the blue-chip index.
Edita posts record quarterly revenue of EGP 7.3 bn, up 32.9%, with profit up 41.5% → volume growth and pricing lift the snack maker, and the stock jumps 7.44%.
Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd move three more Gemini services back to the Suez Canal from December → more Asia-Europe traffic adds to canal revenue and dollar inflows.

key.l: tanker incidents near Hormuz in a week, per Iran

stories.h: Iran strikes US sites in Bahrain as tankers are hit near Hormuz
stories.what: Britain's UKMTO reports two tankers struck by projectiles near Khasab, Oman, on Saturday, with no casualties. Al Jazeera's correspondent counts about 25 incidents reported by Iran's armed forces in a week. Iran's IRGC says it hit US air-defence radars at Bahrain's al-Riffa and Awali bases; Bahrain says a fire broke out at a civilian facility in Sitra with no injuries. Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia continue.
stories.why: The US blockades Iranian ports and Iran answers by targeting shipping and US bases in the Gulf.
stories.aff: Oil supply, tanker insurance, Gulf security and Red Sea shipping.
stories.eg: Higher shipping risk weighs on Suez traffic and Egypt's import and fuel bills.
stories.egx: Bearish for shipping and import-heavy sectors; a risk to sentiment at the open.

key.l: CBE cuts Goldman expects from late Q1 2027 to 2028

stories.h: Goldman sees the CBE holding at 20%, then cutting 700 bp by 2028
stories.what: Goldman Sachs expects the CBE to keep its overnight deposit rate at 20% until late Q1 2027, then cut 500 bp in 2027 and 200 bp in 2028, to 13%. It sees inflation near 14% by year-end and 11.1% in FY2026/27. It raises its dollar forecasts to 53 pounds in three months and 50 in 12 months, says the pound is more than 30% below fair value, and sees no external financing gap through FY2029/30 unless the war escalates. Foreign holdings of local debt are about $20 bn, down from about $30 bn at end-September, while remittances hit a record $38.2 bn in nine months.
stories.why: The CBE hiked 100 bp in October and let the pound weaken; inflation has since slowed to 12.7%.
stories.aff: Interest rates, the pound, bank margins and borrowing costs.
stories.eg: Rates stay high for now, with relief expected in 2027.
stories.egx: Bullish for rate-sensitive sectors over the next year.
stories.names: Talaat Moustafa, Palm Hills, Emaar Misr (bullish).

stories.h: Misr Life targets a 70% payout ahead of its EGX debut
stories.what: Misr Life Insurance offers a 15% stake, with trading due to start in early December; EFG Hermes leads the deal and the Sovereign Fund of Egypt is the ultimate owner. It earned EGP 5.8 bn in 2025, a 19.7% return on equity, and targets a 70% payout from FY2026. Separately, Halan Consumer Finance, part of EGX-listed MNT-Halan, applies to the FRA for an EGP 30 bn securitised bond programme after its loan book grew 42% in nine months.
stories.why: The Sovereign Fund of Egypt is selling part of a state-owned insurer.
stories.aff: Insurance, the EGX's depth and non-bank funding.
stories.eg: A large dividend payer joins the market.
stories.egx: Bullish for brokers and market liquidity.

stories.h: Orascom Construction breaks ground on Jordan's Aqaba-Amman water project
stories.what: Orascom Construction starts work on the $6.7 bn Aqaba-Amman project, which it won in April: an 851k cubic-metre-a-day desalination plant built with France's SUEZ and a 418 km pipeline built with Arab Contractors. Construction takes four years, after which Orascom and SUEZ will run both for 26 years. Orascom's new merger shares list on 24 November.
stories.why: The project should supply water to about 40% of Jordan's population.
stories.aff: Orascom's backlog and Egyptian contractors abroad.
stories.eg: Egyptian firms win large regional infrastructure work.

key.l: EU waste-export ban to non-listed countries

stories.h: EU draft leaves Egypt off its list for metal-scrap exports
stories.what: Egypt asked the European Commission to add it to the first list of non-OECD countries allowed to receive EU metal scrap, but the draft leaves it off. EU waste exports to non-listed countries are banned from 21 May 2027. Brussels is also weighing a bidding ban for foreign firms with distortive subsidies, with a package due on 9 December.
stories.why: The EU is tightening rules on waste exports and subsidised bidders.
stories.aff: Egypt's steelmakers and firms bidding for EU contracts.
stories.eg: Scrap supply for local steel mills could tighten.

key.l: spot gold's fall in the week to 20 Nov

stories.h: Gold ends its worst week in eight months; 21K in Egypt edges up on Sunday
stories.what: Spot gold settles 2.4% lower at $3,538.11 on Friday and loses 8.9% on the week as markets bet on a December Fed hike and AI losses force margin-call selling. Investors next watch the US PCE price index. In Egypt, Banky's 21K price rises EGP 40, or 0.73%, to EGP 5,510 a gram on Sunday.
stories.why: Rate-hike bets and a firm dollar weigh on gold.
stories.eg: Gold stays near its lowest in about a year for Egyptian buyers.

stories.h: EGX reopens after three straight losses and a global sell-off
stories.what: The EGX30 closed Thursday at 51,458.04, down 0.17% and its third loss in a row; turnover was EGP 6.2 bn, 43.9% below the 90-day average. Telecom Egypt (-3.47%) and Orascom Construction (-1.93%) led losses while Edita (+2.94%) gained. Since then Wall Street has fallen into a correction and the Gulf war has widened.
stories.why: The sources give no single cause; the index is still up 23.0% this year.
stories.eg: Sunday's session opens against a weak global backdrop.
stories.egx: Neutral to bearish for the open.
